title: Custom GraphQL scalars in Powerhouse use Zod schemas for validation and must be registered in seven places in scalars.ts
content:
Custom scalars are created in `src/scalars/graphql/` of the document-engineering project. Each scalar file exports (verified in `src/scalars/graphql/AmountMoney.ts` at lines 9, 11, 13, 15, 32, 50): `type` (TS type as string), `typedef` (GraphQL definition e.g. `'scalar PhoneNumber'`), `schema` (Zod validation), `stringSchema` (string representation for code generation), `config` (GraphQLScalarTypeConfig with name, description, serialize/parseValue/parseLiteral), and `scalar` (GraphQLScalarType instance). Registration in `src/scalars/graphql/scalars.ts` requires updating **seven** sections — this note previously listed eight by including a separate "export object" that does not exist. The real seven are: (1) the namespace imports (`import * as Currency from './Currency.js'`), (2) the `export type { ScalarType as XScalarType }` re-exports, then the five exported registries: (3) `customScalars` (line 61), (4) `resolvers` (86), (5) `typeDefs` (107), (6) `generatorTypeDefs` (128) and (7) `validationSchema` (149). There is no separate aggregate export — `customScalars` is the registry. Scalars can be integrated into React components by using `scalar.schema.safeParse(value)` for validation, enabling consistent frontend/backend validation.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against the document-engineering repo at v1.40.5 (`/home/p/Powerhouse/document-engineering`), a separate repo from the powerhouse monorepo._
description: Each scalar exports type, typedef, schema (Zod), stringSchema, config and scalar; registration touches seven sections of scalars.ts — two import/export blocks plus five registries.
